clue.text: Hot meals

parts.note: a plain-looking description of spicy Indian-style dishes, read as a definition of the dish itself

explanation.walkthrough: A very short, almost straight definition: 'hot' carries both senses, heated and spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiced Indian stews are the classic fiery dinner, hot in both temperature and pepper.

clue.text: Go riding around on the wind

indicators.note: the bicycling word is placed around the little word that follows it in the clue

parts.note: to cycle is to go riding on a bike
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a bike ride out in a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts ON inside CYCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating storm system is a kind of wind.

clue.text: Though a little eccentric, he's the most prosperous

indicators.note: only a small part of these words is needed, a run spanning their join

explanation.surface: A rich man is described as somewhat odd but the wealthiest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' signals that the answer lies inside eccentRIC HE'S The.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthiest means having the greatest riches, the top level of wealth.

clue.text: Private hotel bearing the royal insignia

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher seen on postboxes

explanation.surface: A hotel boasts the royal coat of arms over its door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' is an adjective here, as in one's private or personal thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost feelings are personal ones, kept hidden and private.

clue.text: Appearing to suit in a new job

indicators.note: a new version of these words reshuffles their letters

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a suit for a fresh position at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TO SUIT IN A; 'Appearing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation can mean a post or position of employment, as in 'situations vacant'.

clue.text: A charge made by river boards

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the boards is an idiom for the theatre stage

explanation.surface: A fee is levied by the authorities who run the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boards' looks like committees, but it is the theatre floor; 'made by' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The cost of sending a letter is a charge paid for mail delivery.

clue.text: Guy turned about clutching a note with which to get fruit

indicators.note: the rearranged man holds the musical letter tightly inside him
turned about suggests the man's letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: a guy is a chap
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A man spins round with a banknote, ready to buy some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned about' rearranges CHAP to PACH, and 'clutching' puts E inside it; 'a' and 'with which to get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, downy stone fruit is a peach.

clue.text: Having caught the spirit, beat it!

parts.note: snared means trapped or caught
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Someone who has got hold of the booze is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it!' sounds like 'go away' but means 'strike it', an instruction to a drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum with rattling wires is something you play by hitting, so the command to hit it defines it.

clue.text: A number will take a cereal from sheer greed

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A count of people takes grain out of pure gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from sheer' joins; 'number' is a Roman numeral, not a count.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, a grasping form of greed.

clue.text: Withdraw 13,being over-weight

parts.note: refers to the answer at 13 across, meaning more or additional
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pull out because they are too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'being over' puts the 13 across answer above CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull out or remove, as a tooth is withdrawn.

clue.text: The objective of the shy

parts.note: a shy is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at a target, not a timid person

explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' suggests timid people; it is the fairground throwing game.
explanation.definitionFit: At a fairground shy, the hairy nut perched on a post is the target knocked off.

clue.text: A hold-up a worker finds very hard

parts.note: a dam holds up water
a worker is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A worker finds a delay very difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' is not a robbery or delay but a barrier holding water back; 'finds' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant originally meant an unbreakable stone, so it describes something extremely tough.

clue.text: Go too far about an open stretch of water

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fussing over something
a reach is a straight stretch of river

explanation.surface: Someone strays beyond a sensible limit on a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not a reversal or container indicator here but simply a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed one's limits is to stretch beyond what is wise, overdoing it.

clue.text: I laze about and do little, from the sound of it

definitions.text: do little, from the sound of it

indicators.note: about indicates the letters of the preceding words are moved around

explanation.surface: A lazy person admits idling around and achieving nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I LAZE. The definition puns on Doolittle, the surname of the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Pygmalion is surnamed Doolittle, which sounds like 'do little'.

clue.text: More craft turned back, no longer being at the forefront

indicators.note: this phrase places the former partner word in front of the craft word

parts.note: ex means former, something that no longer is

indicators.note: the word for craft is written backwards

parts.note: art is a craft or skill

explanation.surface: Extra boats turned back, as they are no longer leading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' turns ART into TRA, and 'being at the forefront' puts EX ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is something over and above what was there.

clue.text: Once a wall's built it's taken into account

indicators.note: building a wall rearranges its parts into a new structure

parts.note: the 's is a contraction with 'is' and adds no letters

explanation.surface: After a wall has been put up, it is included in the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges ONCE A WALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an allowance for something means taking it into account.

clue.text: Batting badly, get runs and he'll revolt

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: something done badly is in a disordered state, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats poorly and scores runs before rebelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting' gives IN: a batting side in cricket is 'in'. 'badly' rearranges GET RUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel who rises up against authority is someone who revolts.

clue.text: A sight sometimes better seen in pairs

definitions.meaning: glasses are a pair of lenses, so the singular noun comes in pairs and helps seeing

explanation.definitionFit: A grand show is an eye-catching display, and the plural means glasses worn to see better.

clue.text: Well it's not used as a form of transport!

definitions.text: Well it's not used as a form of transport!

parts.words: Well it's not used as a form of transport
parts.note: 'well' is not an interjection but the opposite of ill: this vehicle is for those who are unwell

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' reads as a conversational opener but means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency vehicles carry the sick and injured, not healthy passengers.

clue.text: Maintains a rising pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: stress is pressure

explanation.surface: Someone insists that pressure is building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns STRESS into SSERTS, read up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to state it firmly, insisting it is so.

clue.text: This could well go to a father's head

definitions.text: This could well go to a father's head

parts.words: This could well go to a father's head
parts.note: the father is a Catholic priest, and the thing on his head is his square hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'go to one's head' suggests intoxication or pride; here it is literal headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy sits on a priest's head.

clue.text: Sounds that make a Greek character almost ill

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: Some noises make a person from Greece feel nearly sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of SICK; 'that make' joins. 'Greek character' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Melody and harmony are organised sounds.

clue.text: Cook about 50.plainly on a good diet

indicators.note: the cooking word wraps around the Roman numeral

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A cook of about fifty is clearly eating healthily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside SIMMER. 'plainly' says the dieter visibly looks thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is dieting becomes visibly thinner.

clue.text: Additional provision made by a willing individual

definitions.text: Additional provision made by a willing individual

parts.words: Additional provision made by a willing individual
parts.note: a 'willing individual' is someone making a will, who adds a supplement to it

explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' means making a will, not eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement to a testament adds or changes provisions after it is written.

clue.text: Payment commonly secured by a twister

definitions.meaning: in British slang a ... is one's wages or salary
a threaded fastener that is turned to hold things together

explanation.walkthrough: 'twister' sounds like a swindler, but it is the twisting fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for wages, and a threaded fastener tightened by turning.

clue.text: Being seated, one's given a meal about one and so content

indicators.note: given here tacks the meal part onto the end after the earlier pieces

parts.note: sat means seated
one's is one is, I'S, with the roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for having eaten wraps around the single letter

parts.note: fed, given a meal
I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Seated at the table and served dinner, a person feels pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside FED; 'and so' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well fed leaves someone happy, contented.

clue.text: Set about the French unpleasant conditions

indicators.note: the first word goes around the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the case for poor working conditions in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LE inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy rain mixed with snow makes for nasty weather.

clue.text: Trip over rut in the street so walk stiffly

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: tripping over something sends it tumbling, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a groove in the road and then walks awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip over' rearranges RUT to TRU, and 'in' puts it inside ST; 'so' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger with a stiff, upright gait is to strut.

clue.text: About to accept retiring associate's suite

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the short word takes the other inside

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: to associate is to unite; the 's adds no letters

explanation.surface: An associate who is retiring moves into a suite of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns UNITE into ETINU, and 'to accept' puts it inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite can be a group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: China, where there's many a crime organisation

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, so it stands for many

indicators.note: organising letters means rearranging them in a new order

explanation.surface: In China, there is a lot of organised crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges A CRIME; 'many' gives C, a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is pottery, so china is a ceramic material.

clue.text: The most fusty holy man keeps the accounts

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
tales are accounts or stories

explanation.surface: A very stuffy cleric looks after the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts TALES inside ST. 'accounts' suggests bookkeeping; it means stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusty means stale and musty, so the superlative of one matches the other.

clue.text: Hold spellbound by the hour in a Lent celebration

indicators.note: the abbreviation is put inside the rearranged letters
a celebration stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: hr is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A Lenten festivity keeps people captivated for an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'celebration' rearranges A LENT into ENTAL, and 'in' puts HR inside it; 'by' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate is to grip someone's attention utterly.
